title: P0420 – Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
description: Bank 1 catalytic converter efficiency is below the threshold monitored by the downstream oxygen sensor. Often exhaust leak, aging cat, or O2 sensor issues.
urgencyNote: Usually safe to drive short distances; fix before emissions test or long trips.
causes: Exhaust leak before downstream O2 sensor
Failing upstream or downstream oxygen sensor
Engine running rich or misfiring (damages cat)
Software or fuel trim related efficiency false flag
solutions: Scan for companion codes (misfire, fuel trim, O2)
Inspect exhaust for leaks ahead of the downstream sensor
Graph upstream vs downstream O2: downstream should be relatively steady
Repair misfires and rich/lean conditions before replacing the cat
Replace catalytic converter only after confirming sensors and exhaust integrity

faq.question: Can I drive with a P0420 code?
faq.answer: Usually yes for short trips if the engine runs smoothly. A failing cat or untreated misfire can worsen damage and emissions.

faq.question: Does P0420 always mean a new catalytic converter?
faq.answer: No. Exhaust leaks and oxygen sensors cause many P0420 cases. Confirm efficiency with sensor data before replacing the cat.

faq.question: Will P0420 fail an emissions test?
faq.answer: Often yes if the monitor is complete and the code is stored, or if readiness monitors are not set.
